headline: 1,395 Olongapo Residents Evacuated as Habagat Flooding Worsens
seoTitle: 1,395 Evacuated in Olongapo Amid Habagat Floods | FMB News
seoDescription: Olongapo City reported 1,395 evacuees from 452 families as persistent Habagat rains flooded communities and forced residents to move to safer areas.
deck: Persistent monsoon rains forced hundreds of families into evacuation centers as rivers and drainage systems overflowed across Olongapo City.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Olongapo City reported 1,395 people from 452 families staying in evacuation centers as of 9:30 a.m. Saturday after persistent Southwest Monsoon rains caused widespread flooding.
The latest independently reported city tally is higher than the earlier newsroom brief, which cited just over 1,000 evacuees. FMB News is using the newer 1,395 figure.

sections.heading: Areas affected
paragraphs: Rising rivers and overflow contributed to flooding in communities including West Bajac-Bajac, East Bajac-Bajac, Kalaklan and Santa Rita. Some displaced residents were reported to be staying outside formal evacuation centers because of local conditions.

sections.heading: Flooding and erosion
paragraphs: Minor soil erosion was reported in Kalaklan on Friday afternoon, leaving rocks on a road. Another erosion incident was reported along Napalan Street in Mabayuan, with no injuries reported.
Some roads in the neighboring Subic Bay Freeport were also reported impassable as the monsoon rain continued.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The city began a preemptive evacuation in Santa Rita on Friday afternoon before a river overflowed later that evening. PAGASA said the southwest monsoon was affecting Luzon, including Olongapo.

The independently reviewed reports do not support the bulletin's detailed claims about boats, military trucks, pumps, community kitchens, hygiene kits and preventive antibiotic distribution, so those details are not included here.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Large-scale evacuation is not only a rainfall story. It tests shelter capacity, relief distribution, transport access and the ability of local government to communicate changing risks quickly as water levels and slope conditions evolve.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Watch for updated Olongapo evacuation counts, river and drainage conditions, landslide advisories and additional rainfall warnings from local authorities and PAGASA.
